title: Choose the visual world for the Sengoku map
question: The roll assigned Indigo Cloth: the map as a length of stencil-dyed cotton. Keep it, take my pick or the standard, or re-roll.

options.label: Indigo Cloth
options.lineage: katazome stencil-dyeing and aizome indigo: noren, furoshiki, tenugui
options.thesis: Japan as a bolt of indigo-dyed cotton: every clan is a dye, and conquest is colour soaking across the cloth.
materials: indigo-dyed cotton, deep at the sea and pale at the coast
provinces as resist-dyed fields in natural dyes: bengara red, kariyasu yellow, murasaki purple, yomogi green
each clan a dye colour plus a small stencil pattern (asanoha, kikkō, same dots), so 25 clans stay distinct
unbleached cotton for land held by many small lords; split provinces dyed in kasuri stripes
sashiko running stitches for alliances and province seams
options.viewport: The archipelago fills the window on an indigo ground at 1467; a woven timeline band runs along the bottom with a play button; the year is set large at the corner.
options.risk: Pattern on small provinces can turn noisy; patterns must stay tiny and quiet, and the dyes must still separate at a glance.

raised.raise: The timeline is a woven band: each year's column is threaded in the colours of the clans and their share of provinces, so the whole period's rise and fall reads in one sweep before you press play.
Change leaves a trace: when a province changes hands, the old dye lingers as a fading ghost while the new one soaks in from the conqueror's side.
A live clan roster beside the map, ranked by provinces held that year; fallen clans drop to undyed grey but stay listed.
Points of no return (Ōnin, Okehazama, Honnō-ji, Sekigahara) are marked thresholds on the band, where play slows down.
Urgency may break the grid: as a decisive battle hits, its name sets large across the sea for a moment, then settles into a marker.
Palette law: dyes are only for clans, indigo is only the sea and the ground, undyed cotton only means divided, and red stitching only means war.

options.label: Edo Province Print
options.lineage: Ishikawa Ryūsen's hand-tinted woodblock maps of Japan, 1680s–1700s
options.thesis: The period seen the way Japan first printed itself: sumi linework, hand-tinted provinces and vertical kanji labels.
options.viewport: A printed map sheet with tinted provinces and kanji labels, a printed title cartouche, and the timeline as a margin scale.
options.risk: The most familiar route: an old-map look on cream paper can drift toward the parchment campaign map you said would feel wrong.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.lineage: plankton glowing in a night sea
options.thesis: Territory as living light that flares where armies move and fades behind them.
options.viewport: A dark Japan where campaigns leave glowing wakes.
options.case: Loses both axes: no tie to the Sengoku world, and glow blurs who holds which province.
options.kept: Change leaves a fading trace of what was there before.

options.label: Accretion Disk
options.thesis: History pulled toward unification as matter toward a horizon.
options.viewport: Clans orbit the capital and fall in.
options.case: Loses both axes: abandons the geography the whole product is about.
options.kept: Irreversible thresholds marked on the timeline.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: The daimyo as a ranked cast with name plates and one-line notes.
options.viewport: A roster of warlords ranked by power.
options.case: Loses both axes: cute and game-like, and the roster pushes the map aside.
options.kept: A ranked, finite clan roster whose fallen members turn grey.

options.label: Raygun Layout Desk
options.viewport: Battle names crashing over a broken map.
options.case: Loses both axes: no Sengoku resonance, and illegible as an atlas.
options.kept: Urgent moments may break the grid with type.

options.label: CRT Arcade
options.thesis: Japan as a sixteen-colour sprite map.
options.viewport: A pixel Japan with blinking battle sprites.
options.case: Loses both axes: exactly the game look you ruled out.
options.kept: A strict palette law: each colour has exactly one job.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Each clan a meter, all leaning together on the big battles.
options.viewport: A row of clan meters under a small map.
options.case: Loses both axes: an instrument panel shrinks the map and has no tie to the period.
options.kept: Reading the whole period by sweeping one row: the woven timeline band.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The history-timelapse map, done with full craft: flat clan colours, a slider and an info panel.
canonCard.viewport: A clean political map, a year slider underneath, a details panel on the right.
canonCard.risk: Close to the textbook look you said would feel wrong.
